# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 21 (Bu-Vb Pc21)

**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** 21. Instructing nuns without approval

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ovāda-sikkhāpada* constitutes the twenty-first rule in the Pācittiya chapter of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* (*Bu-Vb Pc21*), establishing an offense of expiation for any monk who instructs nuns without the formal agreement or authorization of the Saṅgha [SuttaCentral]. The rule's origin narrative recounts that the group of six monks (*chabbaggiyā*) went to teach the bhikkhunīs for the sake of material gains, but delivered only a fleeting Dhamma talk before spending the remainder of the day indulging in frivolous conversation, prompting the nuns to complain to the Buddha [Sujato 2009]. In the text of the rule and its early Vinaya context, this instruction is intimately tied to the eight fundamental rules (*garudhammas*), which are reviewed or enquired about prior to formal exhortation (*ovāda*) [Horner 1963; Hüsken 1997]. Commentarial literature, including the *Samantapāsādikā* and rulings cited from the *Mahāpaccarī*, provides detailed expositions of these eight *garudhammas* under Pācittiya 21 and delineates overlapping disciplinary liabilities—such as instructing without Saṅgha consensus, visiting the nuns' quarters after sunset, or delivering the exhortation without proper authorization [Horner 1966; Hüsken 1997].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this training rule is preserved across all major Buddhist vinaya traditions, with Prātimokṣa and Vibhaṅga equivalents found in Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya recensions extant in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also records passage-level parallels in the *Bhikkhunikkhandhaka* of the Cullavagga (Kd 20), the *Gotamīsutta* (AN 8.51), and the *Ovādasutta* (AN 8.52) [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse computation via DharmaNexus corroborates these alignments, identifying substantial shared material between this rule (§3.1.19–3.1.38) and Kd 20 (§1.4.2–1.4.21), as well as with AN 8.51 (§51.11.1–51.18.2) and various other Khandhaka treatises, alongside cross-language matches in the Sanskrit *Pravāraṇāvastu*, Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya*, and Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* [DharmaNexus].
